lit: Bledt et al. (2018)
MIT Cheetah 3: Design and Control of a Robust, Dynamic Quadruped Robot
IEEE/RSJ IROS
Designed high-torque density proprioceptive actuators and Model Predictive Control (MPC) for dynamic walking over rough terrain without vision.
High cost (~$50k+), complex custom planetary gearing, no environmental/agricultural sensing payload.
Kau et al. (2019)
Stanford Doggo: An Open-Source, Quasi-Direct-Drive Quadruped
IEEE ICRA
Developed an open-source 3D-printed quadruped platform using quasi-direct drive brushless motors for dynamic bounding.
Optimized purely for acrobatic jumps/speed; lacks on-board compute for perception and has <10 min battery life.
Katz et al. (2019)
Mini Cheetah: A Hardware Design for Extremity Locomotion
IEEE ICRA
Modular 3-DOF leg design using low-cost backdrivable BLDC motors enabling agile omnidirectional gaits.
Focuses strictly on mechanical agility in laboratory environments; no autonomous navigation or edge AI pipeline.
Hutter et al. (2016)
ANYmal - A Unique Quadruped Robot for Autonomous Operation in Harsh Environments
IEEE/RSJ IROS
Industrial-grade quadruped with series elastic actuators (SEAs) and IP67 ruggedized body for outdoor inspection.
Prohibitively expensive ($100k+), heavy industrial form-factor unsuitable for smallholder precision farming.
Ding et al. (2021)
Learning to Walk on Uneven Terrain for Quadrupedal Robots using Reinforcement Learning
IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO)
Trained neural network locomotion policies in simulation (Isaac Gym) with robust sim-to-real transfer over rugged slopes.
High computational training overhead; policy does not integrate multi-sensor agronomic payloads or path tracking.
Bellicoso et al. (2018)
Dynamic Locomotion Through Online Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrupedal Robots
IEEE Robotics & Automation Letters (RA-L)
Real-time ZMP and CoM trajectory optimization enabling adaptive crawl and trot gaits over unmodeled obstacles.
Requires high-end x86 computer boards; difficult to run concurrently with edge vision models on low-power platforms.
Fehlmann et al. (2023)
Precision Agriculture Using Autonomous Ground Robots: A Review
Springer Precision Agriculture
Systematic review of wheeled and tracked agricultural rovers for weed control, phenotyping, and soil sampling.
Identifies severe mobility failure of wheeled rovers in wet mud, soft soil, and high-crop canopy furrows.
Roldán et al. (2018)
Mini-UAVs and Mobile Robots for Precision Agriculture: A Review of Multi-Robot Systems
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Analyzed complementary roles of aerial drones (macro-surveys) and ground robots (micro-inspection).
Highlighted drone limitations: 20-min flight time, inability to inspect leaf undersides, and blind spots beneath crop canopies.
Bogue, R. (2016)
Robots in Agriculture: State of the Art and Future Directions
Industrial Robot: An International Journal
Surveyed commercial adoption of agricultural robotics, highlighting high ROI in crop health monitoring.
Commercial units are bulky, heavy, cause soil compaction, and require flat structured greenhouse tracks.
Vasconez et al. (2020)
Human–Robot Interaction in Agriculture: A Survey and Review
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Investigated telemetry, UX dashboards, and safety mechanisms for farmer-robot interfaces in open fields.
Found most agricultural robotic interfaces are academic prototypes lacking real-time edge telemetry and alert maps.
Mohanty et al. (2016)
Using Deep Learning for Image-Based Plant Disease Detection
Frontiers in Plant Science
Trained AlexNet and GoogLeNet on 54,306 images across 26 diseases with 99.35% classification accuracy.
Tested only on static laboratory-controlled leaf images with uniform backgrounds; lacks edge device deployment.
Ferentinos, K. P. (2018)
Deep Learning Models for Plant Disease Detection and Diagnosis
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Evaluated VGG, ResNet, and AlexNet on 87,848 leaf images with real-world noise variations (99.5% accuracy).
High parameter count (VGG/ResNet) causes severe latency and memory bottlenecks on embedded single-board computers.
Too et al. (2019)
A Comparative Study of Fine-Tuning Deep Learning Architectures for Plant Disease Identification
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Benchmarked MobileNetV2, DenseNet-121, and InceptionV3; proved MobileNetV2 achieves 97.4% accuracy with 10× fewer FLOPs.
Did not perform hardware-specific quantization (TensorRT / ONNX) or test real-time video stream ingestion.
Chen et al. (2020)
Using Deep Transfer Learning for Image-Based Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Devices
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Deployed lightweight CNN on Raspberry Pi 3B+ using INT8 quantization, achieving 12 FPS at 92.1% accuracy.
Insufficient FPS for continuous mobile robot navigation; no integration with robotic gait or sensor fusion.
Saleem et al. (2019)
Plant Disease Detection and Classification by Deep Learning: A Review
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Comprehensive meta-analysis of deep learning architectures, dataset biases, and real-time field challenges.
Concluded that field-ready solutions require mobile ground robots that bring cameras within 0.5m of plant leaves.
Internet of Things for Smart Agriculture: Technologies, Practices and Future Direction
Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Smart Environments
Proposed layered IoT architecture for soil moisture, microclimate, and particulate monitoring in precision farming.
Relied exclusively on stationary sensor nodes (motes), creating spatial coverage gaps across large farm tracts.
Elijah et al. (2018)
An Overview of Internet of Things (IoT) and Data Analytics in Smart Agriculture
IEEE Internet of Things Journal
Investigated wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and cloud data pipelines for environmental anomaly detection.
High infrastructure cost of deploying hundreds of stationary nodes; vulnerable to field vandalism and weather damage.
Bacco et al. (2019)
Smart Farming: Technologies, Applications and Challenges in Precision Agriculture
Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier)
Explored multi-sensor data fusion (temperature, humidity, organic gases, optical imagery) for soil health profiling.
Lacked mobile autonomous platforms to transport multi-sensor payloads dynamically throughout crop rows.
